blindSummary: This state/province — a city-status unit rather than one of the country's full autonomous units — has no regional LGBTQ+ or gender-identity statute, a framework gap shared with two neighbouring units and recorded in the country's national inventory of sub-national legislation as a gap case only. No incident evidence, no enforcement data, and no hate-offence figure separating this unit from the national aggregate was retrievable; this is a statute-book gap, explicitly not an incident finding. The unit's distinctive religious-demographic composition (recognised minority faith communities under their own autonomous arrangements) and the heavily fenced international border-crossing environment create a document-and-presentation context different from the country's other units, adding modest friction for a visitor whose identity documents do not match presentation. National criminal law and the national police forces still operate here, so the enforcement floor is unchanged; unlike two neighbouring units with their own police forces, this state/province has no regional equality office, LGBTQ+ observatory, or own police force.
blindSourceSummaries: A national LGBTQ+ federation's September 2025 report on LGBTQ+ education policy across the country's units (co-authored with a public university; front matter retrieved): its comparative inventory of regional LGBTQ+ legislation is the source that places this unit among those with no regional LGBTQ+ statute.

An index page of the country's sub-national LGBTQ+ legislation; lists each unit's law and states expressly that this unit (and one neighbour) has no regional LGBTQ+ statute of its own and must instead apply the national equality framework and central-government policies.
